newsitem.title: USA: SCANA Q1 trimmed by warm weather.
newsitem.headline: SCANA Q1 trimmed by warm weather.

text.p: SCANA Corp said Monday unusually mild weather reduced first quarter earnings $0.10 per share.

The company reported earnings for the latest quarter of $57.4 million, or $0.54 per share, down from $68.8 million, or $0.66 per share, in the first quarter of 1996. Earnings for the first quarter of 1996 included a one-time gain of $0.05 per share related to the Company's investment in InterCel, Inc, an established telecommunications company that is developing a wireless personal communications services system in the Southeast.

"Our first quarter results reflect unusually mild weather that led to lower sales of electricity by South Carolina Electric & Gas Co, our principal subsidiary," said Kevin B. Marsh, SCANA's chief financial officer.

"Heating degree days in SCE&G's electric service territory for the quarter were 30 percent below the first quarter of 1996 and 27 percent below the 30-year normal for the period," said Marsh. "The impact of the milder weather reduced earnings in the first quarter by $0.10 per share compared to the first quarter of last year, when we experienced colder than normal weather."

Territorial kilowatt-hour sales of electricity were down 4.4 percent for the quarter. Residential and commercial sales were down 12.5 percent and 1.5 percent respectively, while industrial sales were up 1.8 percent.

"The milder weather had the most impact on residential sales," said Marsh. "However, we were pleased to see that industrial sales continue to grow, reflecting the strength in our service area economy."
Marsh noted that depreciation and property taxes increased compared to the first quarter of last year, while operating and maintenance expenses declined slightly.

South Carolina Pipeline Corp, SCANA's natural gas transmission company, earned $0.04 per share in the first quarter, up from $0.02 per share last year primarily as a result of increased sales to industrial customers.
SCANA Petroleum Resources, the company's oil and natural gas exploration and production subsidiary, contributed $0.03 per share to first quarter earnings.
